chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Stan Kenton's tribute tune and "The Peanut Vendor"
summary: Kenton recorded "Machito" after the concert; Machito's rhythm section then played on Kenton's "Peanut Vendor" at Capitol, working in harmony with drummer Shelly Manne.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Uh - Huh. Okay, in 1947, in February, Stan Kenton recorded a tune called "Machito", where he paid you tribute. Do you remember that?

Now, I understand he saw that January 24 concert, so that means he must have had Pete Rugalo write that tune within two or three weeks and he recorded it three weeks later. Ahhh, how does that make you feel, somebody paying that kind of tribute to you?
Such a great musician like, because he was a perfectionist. He was very, very dedicated and he has a young musician that was something else, good musician, good legitimate musician.
Did he ever tell you why he wrote that tune, "Machito"?
He was so grateful for all the, of the cooperation from Rene, Mario Bauza, Vidal .....
.... for introducing a new sound or did you help him out with ....
No. We helped him, we helped him out tremendously, because he fell in love with our rhythm section.....

.... because, well, we was, I mean could play to impress Duke Ellington or Count Basie, musically. Practically everything was coming from them. If it wasn't note by note, the idea was there, so they was so grateful about the our contribution with the rhythm section and we went up there and we catered to them because we never fight with his rhythm section.
They recorded "The Peanut Vendor" that same year.
Now, did you or any of your men take part of that recording, "The Peanut Vendor"?

Carlos Vidal. So the rhythm section was there and we didn't fight with (Shelly) Manne, the drummmer, we catered to him. He was - he flipped because he says, "Gee, I thought that I was going to have a problem with the conga players", because for him it was something new.
Where did you record that, here or in California?
No, here at the, those studios in Odd-Fellow Temple, 106th and Park Ave.
I see. Were you satisfied the way "The Peanut Vendor" came out?
